scope: One row per encyclical from Benedict XIV (1740) to the present. The base list is every record typed "encyclical" in src/sources/papal-documents/catalog.json, the catalogue built from the Vatican's formal document indexes (325 records, Benedict XIV through Leo XIV), less 3 index rows withheld as probable duplicates of other rows (vernacular incipits of the same acts): "Fin dal primo momento" (1922-12-23); "Rappresentanti in terra" (1929-12-31); "Nos es muy conocida" (1937-03-28). Three Pius IX apostolic letters that the Italian index alone labels "Enciclica" are not included. No additions beyond the catalogue have been reviewed yet. readers[] lists every installed reading PDF in release/papal-documents.json that is a witness of the row's act: Latin or other original-language printings, and historical English translations printed by 1930. A row without a reader carries a Vatican link and the reason no local text is offered. English routes separately identify publicly readable human English translations, their host, checked date and complete, fragmentary or damaged extent. An external English link does not establish a local republication right or an installed PDF.

description_provenance.author: Claude (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI), AI-written project apparatus
description_provenance.method: The first 255 descriptions were written by Claude after reading the act's own text: for rows with an installed reader, the reader's selected source text (opening, section headings and a mid-text sample), preferring a complete English witness, then Latin; otherwise the Vatican page in English, Latin or Italian. description_basis names the text read. Descriptions are neutral summaries of the act's main concern, at most 160 characters, and are not papal wording. Codex wrote the remaining 67 descriptions after inspecting the opening, headings and representative central passages of 66 official English texts and the official Italian Orientales Ecclesias. Each description_basis identifies the actual text used; the descriptions are original project summaries, not translations of the acts.
